portName: Port of Monaco (Port Hercule, Rainier III breakwater)
seoTitle: Monaco cruise port guide: Port Hercule, lifts and buses
seoDescription: Monaco cruise port 2026: dock at Port Hercule, Casino 10–12 min and Monaco-Ville 15–20 min on foot. Free lifts, CAM bus €2, Bateau Bus, train to Nice 25 min.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the cruise terminal on the Rainier III breakwater in Port Hercule, or anchor off and tender in when the berth is taken. Monaco-Ville and the Casino are each 10–20 minutes on foot with free public lifts; CAM buses cost €2 from the driver or €1.50 by card (2026). Be back an hour before all-aboard, 90 minutes if you tender or go to Nice by train.
intro: Monaco is the rare port where the ship ties up in the middle of the country. The cruise terminal sits on the floating breakwater of Port Hercule, below the Rock of Monaco-Ville on one side and Monte-Carlo on the other, so the whole day can be done on foot. The catch is height: the Palace, the Oceanographic Museum and the Casino all sit well above the harbour, and the free public lifts and escalators make the difference between a pleasant day and a sweaty one. Since 2020 Monaco has accepted only luxury and premium ships of up to 250 m and 1,250 passengers. If your ship is bigger, your 'Monaco' call is probably at Villefranche, about 45 minutes away by coach.
tenderNotes: Ships normally berth at the Rainier III breakwater. When the berth is taken, or a ship is scheduled for the roadstead, it anchors off Port Hercule and runs its own tenders into the harbour; the crossing takes a few minutes. Afternoon queues for return tenders can be long. Check the last tender time in your daily programme and allow an extra 30 minutes.

terminals.name: Monaco cruise terminal (Rainier III breakwater, Port Hercule)
terminals.notes: The 352 m semi-floating breakwater on the outer side of Port Hercule. Takes ships up to 300 m in principle, though government policy limits calls to ships of 250 m and 1,250 passengers. The terminal handles security and passenger controls and supports turnaround calls. Monaco-Ville is about 700 m and the Casino about 850 m from the terminal gate.

terminals.name: Port de Fontvieille
terminals.notes: A yacht marina on the far side of the Rock, limited to boats with a 3 m draught. It is not a cruise berth. Fontvieille is worth knowing only as a district: CAM lines 3, 4 and 6 start there.

walkability.detail: From the terminal gate, Place du Casino is about 850 m (10–12 minutes) and Monaco-Ville about 700 m but 15–20 minutes because of the climb. The Oceanographic Museum, Palace and Cathedral are all on the Rock, about 20 minutes away. Free public lifts and escalators link the levels; the lifts up to Monaco-Ville are reached from Avenue des Corsaires. Monaco-Monte-Carlo station is about 1.3 km away and harder to find on foot.

transportSections.time: 10–20 min to Monaco-Ville or the Casino
transportSections.detail: The quickest way around. Pick up a lift map at the terminal before you set off; Monaco is a city of lifts and escalators between levels, and they save a lot of climbing.

transportSections.cost: €2 paid on board; €1.50 by bank card or Monapass app (2026)
transportSections.detail: Crosses Port Hercule between Quai Antoine 1er (Monaco-Ville side) and Quai des États-Unis (Monte-Carlo side), saving about a kilometre of walking. Departures roughly every 20 minutes from each side, 08:00–20:00.

transportSections.cost: €2 from the driver, valid 30 minutes for a connection; €1.50 by card or Monapass app; €5.50 day pass (2026)
transportSections.detail: Six day lines, about 07:00–21:00. Lines 1 and 2 both serve Monaco-Ville and Monte-Carlo; lines 5 and 6 go to Larvotto beach. Pay the driver or use contactless or the app. In 2026 the whole network was free during major events, including the Grand Prix week (1–8 June) and the Monaco Yacht Show (18–30 September).

transportSections.mode: SNCF regional train (TER) to Nice or Menton
transportSections.cost: Buy at the station machines or in the SNCF Connect app; check the fare before you travel
transportSections.time: About 22–25 min to Nice-Ville; about 10 min to Menton
transportSections.detail: Monaco-Monte-Carlo station is underground, reached by escalators and lifts, about 20–25 minutes on foot from the terminal; a bus or taxi is easier. Trains on the coast line also stop at Èze-sur-Mer, but Èze village is on a hilltop far above that station.

transportSections.cost: Metered; ask for an estimate first
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait at the pier, generally until early evening. Worth it for Èze or for anyone who struggles with hills. Rideshare pickups in Monaco are not reliable.
Starts just outside the cruise terminal. Useful if you want to see the main sights without climbing.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board an hour before all-aboard if docked (16:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard); 90 minutes before if your ship is tendering or you went to Nice by train.
returnTiming.detail: Nothing in Monaco is more than about 20–25 minutes on foot from the terminal, but the walk down from Monaco-Ville or Monte-Carlo is steep in places and lifts can queue. From Nice, the train takes 22–25 minutes and the station is 20–25 minutes from the terminal, so be on a train from Nice-Ville at least 2 h 15 min before all-aboard (15:15 for a 17:30 all-aboard). On tender days, return tenders fill up in the afternoon.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If you miss a train in Nice, take the next one; trains on the coast line are frequent at peak times. A taxi from Nice is slower than the train in traffic. In Monaco, taxis wait at the pier until early evening. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you will be late.

excursionAdvice: Monaco itself does not need an excursion. With an extra hour, the Jardin Exotique above Fontvieille reopened on 30 March 2026 after six years of works; tickets from €12, CAM line 2. It is small, safe and well served by lifts, and a self-guided walk covers the Palace, Cathedral, Oceanographic Museum and Casino in a day. A ship tour earns its price for Èze, which is awkward by public transport, for a combined Èze and Nice day, or for anyone who cannot manage the hills. If your ship is actually calling at Villefranche, the ship's coach to Monaco takes away the transport question.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at the Rainier III breakwater at 08:00. On a tender day, start 30 minutes later and finish 30 minutes earlier.

steps.what: Leave the terminal and walk along the harbour towards Avenue des Corsaires; take the public lifts up to Monaco-Ville.
Walk the lanes of the Rock and visit Monaco Cathedral, where Princess Grace and Prince Rainier are buried.
Oceanographic Museum, on the cliff edge of the Rock. Allow 90 minutes.
Palace Square for the changing of the guard at 11:55. Arrive early for a front spot.

Walk down to La Condamine and lunch at the Marché de la Condamine on Place d'Armes. The covered hall is closed for refurbishment from January 2026 for about 13 months, so the stalls are outside on the square.
Bateau Bus across the harbour to Quai des États-Unis.

Walk up to Place du Casino: the Casino de Monte-Carlo from outside, the Hôtel de Paris and the Casino gardens. The Casino's sightseeing visit runs only 10:00–13:00 (last entry 12:15, €19), so to go inside, swap this with the Rock and start at the Casino at 10:00.
Walk back down past the harbour and the yachts, following part of the Grand Prix circuit.
Back on board, an hour before all-aboard.

sights.name: Prince's Palace and the changing of the guard
sights.why: The Grimaldi family's palace on the Rock; the guard changes daily at 11:55 in Palace Square.
sights.timeNeeded: 30 minutes for the ceremony; 1 hour with the State Apartments
sights.cost: Free to watch the guard; State Apartments charged, open April–October only (closed from 15 October 2026)
sights.tip: The State Apartments open from April to October and close from 15 October in 2026; on a late-autumn call you see the palace from the square only.

sights.name: Oceanographic Museum
sights.why: Marine science museum and aquarium built into the cliff on the seaward side of the Rock.
sights.tip: The best wet-day choice in Monaco, and close to the Cathedral and Palace.

sights.name: Monaco Cathedral
sights.why: 19th-century Romanesque-revival cathedral where Princess Grace and Prince Rainier III are buried.
sights.tip: It is a short walk from the Oceanographic Museum, on the way to the Palace.

sights.name: Monaco-Ville (the Rock)
sights.why: The old town: narrow lanes, ramparts and views over Port Hercule and Fontvieille.
sights.tip: Use the public lifts from Avenue des Corsaires to avoid the steepest climbs.

sights.name: Casino de Monte-Carlo and Place du Casino
sights.why: The belle époque casino and square, with the Hôtel de Paris and Café de Paris alongside.
sights.cost: Exterior, square and gardens free; sightseeing visit €19, 10:00–13:00, last entry 12:15 (2026)
sights.tip: The sightseeing visit is mornings only, so go at 10:00 if you want to see inside. Smart-casual dress is enforced for the gaming rooms: no shorts, flip-flops, beachwear or sportswear. Bring your passport.

sights.name: Port Hercule and the Grand Prix circuit
sights.why: Superyachts in the harbour and the street circuit around it, including the harbour-front straight and the tunnel road.
sights.tip: Walk it on the way back to the ship; the Bateau Bus cuts out the long loop around the harbour.

sights.name: Èze village (excursion)
sights.why: Medieval hilltop village on the road between Monaco and Nice, with a cactus garden at the top and wide sea views.
sights.tip: The train only reaches Èze-sur-Mer on the coast, far below the village. A taxi or ship tour is much simpler.

beaches.name: Larvotto
beaches.howToGetThere: CAM line 5 or 6 to the Larvotto terminus, or walk east along the seafront.
beaches.time: About 25–30 min on foot from the port; shorter by bus
beaches.cost: Free public beach; paid beach clubs along it
beaches.note: Monaco's main public beach and the only real beach option within the principality.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming your ship docks in Monaco.
commonMistakes.fix: Monaco only takes ships of up to 250 m and 1,250 passengers. Larger ships call at Villefranche, about 45 minutes away by coach. Check your itinerary.

commonMistakes.mistake: Climbing to Monaco-Ville or the Casino on foot in the heat.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the free public lifts and escalators. Ask for a lift map at the terminal.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at the Casino gaming rooms in shorts.
commonMistakes.fix: Smart-casual dress is enforced and you need your passport. The square and gardens have no dress code.

commonMistakes.mistake: Missing the changing of the guard.
commonMistakes.fix: It is at 11:55 daily. Arrive at Palace Square by about 11:30 for a view.

commonMistakes.mistake: Cutting the return from Nice too fine.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow for the 20–25 minute walk from Monaco-Monte-Carlo station to the terminal, or take a bus or taxi.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to get to Èze village by train.
commonMistakes.fix: Èze-sur-Mer station is at sea level; the village is on a hilltop above it. Take a taxi or a tour.

safety: Monaco is one of the safest places in Europe to spend a port day, with heavy police presence and CCTV. The usual care applies in crowds at Palace Square and Place du Casino. The bigger risks are outside the principality: pickpocketing is common on the regional trains along the coast and at Nice-Ville station. Steep streets, steps and traffic on the narrow roads are the main physical hazards.
scams: Pickpockets on the Nice–Monaco–Menton regional trains and at Nice-Ville station, especially on crowded summer trains. Keep bags zipped and in front, and phones out of back pockets.
Unclear taxi fares for trips out of Monaco, for example to Èze or Nice. Ask for an estimate before you get in and make sure the meter runs.
Card terminals and cash machines offering to charge you in your home currency. Choose euros to avoid a poor exchange rate.
accessibility: The cruise terminal and the harbour front are level, and Monaco's public lifts and escalators make most of the principality reachable without stairs, including Monaco-Ville from Avenue des Corsaires. Confirm that the lifts you need are working before relying on them. Monaco-Ville's lanes are smooth but sloping in places. On tender days, boarding a tender depends on the sea state, and wheelchair users may not be able to go ashore; ask the ship. CAM buses and the Bateau Bus are a useful alternative to steep walks.
rainyDay: The Oceanographic Museum is the best wet-day choice and can fill a morning. Monaco Cathedral and the Palace State Apartments, when open, are indoors and close together on the Rock. The Casino atrium and the covered arcades around Place du Casino are good for a dry hour. The Bateau Bus and CAM buses keep walking in the rain to a minimum.
crowdTips: Cruise crowds are modest because Monaco accepts only smaller ships: 99 calls and about 70,300 passengers in July–September 2025. Most visitors on the Rock come by coach from Nice and Villefranche, and Palace Square fills up well before the 11:55 changing of the guard. Place du Casino is busiest from late morning. Event weeks transform the city: in 2026 the Grand Prix fell on 1–8 June and the Monaco Yacht Show on 18–30 September, with road closures but free buses.

faqs.q: Where do cruise ships dock in Monaco?
faqs.a: At the cruise terminal on the Rainier III breakwater in Port Hercule, below Monaco-Ville. Fontvieille is a yacht marina, not a cruise berth.
Usually not; ships dock at the breakwater. When the berth is taken or the ship is scheduled for the roadstead, it anchors off Port Hercule and tenders in. Your daily programme will say which.

faqs.q: Is Monaco walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Place du Casino is 10–12 minutes and Monaco-Ville 15–20 minutes on foot, with free public lifts and escalators to help with the climbs.

faqs.q: How do I get from Monaco cruise port to Monte-Carlo?
faqs.a: Walk around the harbour and up to Place du Casino in about 10–12 minutes, or take the Bateau Bus across the harbour to Quai des États-Unis (€2 on board, €1.50 by card, 2026).

faqs.q: How much is the bus in Monaco?
faqs.a: CAM buses cost €2 from the driver, €1.50 by bank card or the Monapass app, and €5.50 for a day pass (2026).

faqs.q: Can I go to Nice from Monaco cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Regional trains from Monaco-Monte-Carlo take about 22–25 minutes. The station is 20–25 minutes on foot from the terminal, so allow plenty of time for the return.

faqs.q: How do I get to Èze from Monaco?
faqs.a: Taxi or ship tour is simplest. The train only reaches Èze-sur-Mer on the coast; the village itself is on a hilltop high above it.

faqs.q: What can I do in Monaco in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk up to Monaco-Ville for the Cathedral, the Oceanographic Museum and the 11:55 changing of the guard, cross the harbour on the Bateau Bus, and finish at Place du Casino.
